title: Proving LinkedIn Attribution for a $500K/Qtr SaaS Client

metrics.label: Closed Won Revenue Attributed to LinkedIn

problem: A large SaaS client running $500K/quarter in LinkedIn media couldn't connect ad exposure to closed-won revenue. With the agency seeing zero measurable ROAS, LinkedIn appeared to be the most expensive and lowest-performing channel in the mix — leading the team to cut spend entirely.
strategy: I established weekly syncs across two tracks: internally with the Sales pod, Product, and Measurement teams to align on how to prove ROAS; externally with the ad agency to audit the original campaign setup and share high-level insights at each touchpoint. We identified LinkedIn's attribution script — which joins CRM data with member-level exposure data to trace the full purchase funnel — as the right solution. The analysis normally carries a 4-week SLA. Given the urgency of the paused spend, I prioritized a 3-day turnaround.
result: The analysis showed that 30% of all closed-won revenue had been influenced by LinkedIn exposure — up from the 0% the client had previously measured. It also revealed that the buying cycle for LinkedIn-exposed prospects was 90 days versus 156 days for unexposed prospects, a 42% reduction. With clear ROAS evidence in hand, the client reinstated their full $500K quarterly budget and the sales team was able to close a critical revenue gap.
takeaway: Cross-functional partnership was essential — without alignment across Sales, Product, Measurement, and the agency, this analysis never gets prioritized or trusted. Being the strategy SME in the room built credibility on both sides. Equally important: I didn't just pull the data and build a deck. I walked the client through the findings and provided clear recommendations on how to move forward, which made the difference between a report and a decision.
